newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher after rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher after rate decision.

text.p: Israeli shares rose on Tuesday to a new all-time high following the decision of the Bank of Israel to leave its key lending rate for August unchanged, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.42 percent, or 1.27 points, to 305.55 on a high all-share turnover of 226 million shekels against 195 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.63 percent higher at 313.54.

"Since there was no surprise and the Bank of Israel did not raise the rates the market can return to normal behavior, meaning that it can resume its rise," said Idan Azoulay at Impact Union Protfolio Management.
After the close of trading on Monday the Bank of Israel announced it would leave its key lending rate for August unchanged at an annual 12.7 percent.
"We were all expecting an unchanged rate but it is still good to hear it," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeler Eblagon Securites. "The mood is very positive and all portfolio managers are buying."
"The session opened with a mild decline but then the market rebounded. This, together with the fact that volume remains high indicates that the makret is very strong," Azoulay said.

Eidelheit said that in the near term the market will continue to rise. "I believe that the market will continue to rise until the Maof reaches 325. Then a correction will come and investors will have to start looking for reasons for another rise," he said.

Azoulay added that investors are now waiting for the release of the July consumer price index on August 15. "Analysts expect a CPI of around one percent which is relatively high for the summer months. A higher than expected figure might lead to a rate hike and the positive trend might change," Azoulay said.
Koor Industries, the most active share, lost 1.0 percent to 38,297 agorot (Israeli cents) on volume of 15.1 million shekels.
Lehman Brothers said Claridge Israel's purchase of a 10.2 percent stake in Koor was a positive development.

Claridge last week paid $187 million for half of Shamrock's 20.4 percent stake with a 90-day option to buy the remaining half for the same price. Claridge acquired another 1.6 percent off the floor for $30 million.

Other active shares include Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which slipped 2.25 percent to 21,905 agorot on volume of 12.2 million shekels; and Bank Leumi, which gained 1.75 percent to 577 agorot on turnover of 10.3 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233 DMG SAS
